app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90 — `group.users.delete(user_id)` executes the DELETE on the has_many-through join row immediately when called, so the following `if group.save` guards nothing: a save failure renders render_json_error while the membership removal has already been committed and cannot be rolled back, misrepresenting server state to the client (confidence 75, P1).

app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:73 — `group.add(user)` inside the each-loop persists each has_many-through join row immediately per iteration, so the trailing `if group.save` is an illusion of transactionality: if save later fails, already-added members remain in the group while the response tells the client the whole add_members call failed (confidence 75, P1).

app/assets/javascripts/admin/routes/admin_group_route.js:13 — removing afterModel and invoking `model.findMembers()` without returning it from setupController drops the promise from Ember's route lifecycle, so a failed members fetch (403/500) is silently swallowed instead of triggering the route's error substate, leaving the admin group page rendered with no member data and no error indication (confidence 75, P2).

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6:11 — the same unreturned `model.findMembers()` call in setupController means the members route commits its transition and renders before the AJAX response arrives and drops any request failure instead of surfacing it through Ember's loading/error substates, a regression from the previous afterModel-based blocking load (confidence 75, P2).

app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:19 — totalPages is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which is off by one at exact multiples of limit (e.g. user_count=50, limit=50 yields totalPages=2 instead of the correct 1), so showingLast stays false and the admin can click "next" into a genuinely empty page (confidence 100, P2).

app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — `limit`/`offset` are coerced with bare `.to_i` and never clamped: a negative offset (e.g. offset=-1) reaches `group.users.order(...).limit(limit).offset(offset)` and raises a Postgres "OFFSET must not be negative" error (500), and an arbitrarily large limit lets a client materialize an entire group's membership (including huge automatic groups) in one request, defeating the pagination design (confidence 75, P2).

app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:25 — `total = group.users.count` and the subsequent `members = group.users.order(...).limit(limit).offset(offset)` are two non-atomic queries, so a concurrent membership add/remove between them desynchronizes meta.total from the returned members page (confidence 50, P3).

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes GroupsController#members from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (a flat JSON array) to `render json: { members: ..., meta: { total, limit, offset } }`, with no backward-compatible alternative in the controller. Internally, the Ember code is updated to expect `result.members`/`result.meta` (e.g., `Group#findMembers` sets `members` from `result.members` and uses `result.meta.*`), but the diff itself provides no compatibility layer for any other consumers that might still expect an array response from `/groups/:group_id/members.json`.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the diff shows `group.users.delete(user_id)` is executed before the `if group.save` conditional. The association deletion call mutates the database immediately, and there is no transaction/rollback logic shown. Therefore, if `group.save` were to fail (e.g., due to validations/callbacks), the controller would render an error even though the membership removal already occurred, causing server/client state mismatch. The `group.save` guard does not actually protect the delete operation.

adjudication.rationale: In `add_members`, the code mutates membership inside the loop via `group.add(user)` and only afterwards decides success/failure based on `if group.save` (new method in this diff). adjudication.rationale: In spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb, the new tests for automatic groups (`.add_members` and `.remove_member`) only assert `response.status.should == 422` and do not verify that the group’s user membership count/contents remain unchanged.
